hypothesis.title: The Uncollapsed Accompaniment
hypothesis.question: Does delaying commitment across harmony, melody, voicing, and hidden timbral signature make accompaniment feel more inevitable, personal, and conversational than an early-collapse workflow?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If a short piece composes accompaniment first as a latent field—harmonic graph adjacency, personal griff palette, coupled melody-harmony cells, subtle phase/signature layer, and call-response timing—then a phrase-boundary collapse version will be rated as more inevitable, personally authored, and conversationally alive than versions that choose chords first or remove the stylistic fingerprint. The mechanism is uncollapsed accompaniment: a constrained possibility field that shapes the audible surface before it becomes one thing.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: S1 shows that real physical transitions choose local accessible phases from a much larger possibility space, with path/rate/pressure affecting the resulting form. S2 supplies the harmonic possibility field: Tonnetz and combinatorial configurations define adjacency and resource structure before a progression is chosen. S6 shows that basso continuo realization contains measurable personal style inside rule-bound improvisation, making accompaniment a fingerprinted field rather than neutral rule execution. S5 adds the strongest formal analogy: coupled melody-harmony generation should remain coherent until measurement, because premature readout destroys the intended advantage. S3 shows that hidden phase/log-magnitude structure can carry robust information below ordinary perceptual attention, suggesting a subtle signature layer for musical identity. S4 grounds the result in practical arrangement, where call-and-response at multiple levels turns latent possibility into audible dialogue [S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6].

recipe.title: Latent Continuo Field Study
recipe.bodyMd: Create a 120-second piece whose accompaniment is composed first as a constrained possibility field and only collapsed into notes phrase by phrase. Draw a 7–12 node harmonic graph and mark three pressure edges usable only near section boundaries [S1, S2]. Define 6–10 modern griffs—recurring voicing gestures with tendencies rather than fixed rules [S6]. For each phrase, score a two-note melodic cell and two-chord harmonic cell together before committing either to MIDI, preserving coupled choice until a phrase boundary [S5]. Add a subtle phase, all-pass, adjacent-bin EQ, ring-mod, or filtered-noise signature that encodes the current griff identity without dominating perception [S3]. Arrange lead/accompaniment gestures as call and response at beat, phrase, bassline, and section levels [S4]. Render Uncollapsed Field, Early Collapse, and No Fingerprint versions, then blind-rate inevitability, personality, and conversational aliveness.
dawChecklist: Create a 7–12 node chord graph before writing the progression.
Mark three pressure edges that can only be used near section boundaries.
Design 6–10 modern griffs as recurring voicing gestures with tendencies.
For each phrase, choose the two-note melody cell and two-chord harmonic cell together.
Score candidate cells for tonal stability, melodic implication, voice-leading distance, and griff identity before committing to MIDI.
Add a subtle phase/all-pass/EQ/ring-mod/noise signature that tracks current griff identity.
Arrange call-and-response between lead and accompaniment at beat and phrase levels.
Render Uncollapsed Field with graph, griffs, coupled cells, signature, and call-response timing active.
Render Early Collapse by choosing chords first, then adding melody and voicing afterward with the same sounds.
Render No Fingerprint by keeping graph and notes but randomizing griffs and removing the hidden signature layer.
Blind-rate all versions for inevitability, personality, and conversational aliveness on a 1–7 scale.

protocol.listeningContext: studio headphones or monitors; loudness matched before rating
protocol.listeningMethod: blind shuffled comparison with 1–7 ratings for inevitability, personality, and conversational aliveness
whatVaries: phrase-boundary collapse versus early chord-first commitment
